rules.title: The catalog decides, the model narrates
rules.body: Tool-to-platform verdicts come from a curated matrix by lookup, never from live model reasoning on the critical path. Language models write the explanations; they do not cast the votes.

rules.title: The model never computes money
rules.body: It selects the inputs. A pure function returns the figure. Every number in section 05 can be recomputed by hand at the table, which is why the formula is shown next to each line.

rules.title: Confidence is a band, not a decimal
rules.body: High — observed directly in your system or invoices. Medium — inferred from consistent evidence. Low — stated once, unverified. A "87% match" is a claim nobody can defend in a room full of people who know their own business.

gaps.source: Aurora Solar, mentioned on the call
Two operator portals, done by hand

prose.recommendation: Start with Airtable and Sortly. They carry the least process risk, they are month-to-month, and cutting them in the first four weeks returns $389 a month while the team learns the platform on data that cannot break an installation.

findings.heading: Five of your seven tools are covered by the platform you would run anyway
findings.body: HubSpot, Airtable, Sortly, Jobber and Zendesk together cost $2,043 a month. Every capability Voltix actually uses in them maps onto an Open Mercato module — three of them natively, two with configuration only. None of the five requires a bespoke module.

findings.heading: One genuine gap: the quote builder
findings.body: Generating a customer quote from a panel-and-inverter configuration is the only thing Voltix does that the platform does not already do. We estimate 40 hours. It is the single largest piece of new code in the programme, and it is a small one.

findings.heading: Two things we recommend you keep
findings.body: Xero stays: statutory books and VAT filing are not a platform problem, and replacing an accounting system to save $78 a month is a bad trade. Legally binding e-signature stays with PandaDoc, wired into the platform through its API rather than rebuilt.

findings.heading: The HubSpot contract sets the timetable
findings.body: Your HubSpot term renews on 28 February 2027 and is the only annual commitment in the stack. A programme starting in October reaches the CRM cut-over in week 10 — comfortably before the renewal decision, which is the point of sequencing it second rather than first.

findings.heading: Four usage statements we could not map
findings.body: Panel-layout design, utility interconnection filings, subsidy paperwork and payroll export sit outside our catalog. They are listed in Appendix B rather than folded into a percentage. Two of them may turn out to be real scope; we would rather find that out with you than around you.

prose.basisIntro: Everything below derives from material you supplied. Where we inferred rather than observed, the confidence band on the row says so.
prose.disclaimer: It is not a proposal to replace your stack. It is an ordered list of pieces worth cutting, each with what it saves and what it costs to cut. You can stop after any wave and keep the savings banked to that point.

waveNotes.body: Installer certifications, site surveys and permit tracking become custom entities in the data designer. The two warehouses move to the wms module with the existing barcode flow. Lowest process risk in the stack: flat data, few users, nothing on the critical path of an installation.

Contacts, deals and pipeline stages move to customers + sales, with the email log imported. Runs in parallel with HubSpot for two weeks before the switch. Completing this before 28 February 2027 is what removes the annual renewal from the table.

Crew scheduling and job sheets move to the planner with your dispatch rules expressed as business rules rather than as habits. Crews run one full week on both systems before Jobber is cancelled — this is the wave the installers actually feel.

Post-install tickets and warranty claims move to messages + warranty_claims. The quote builder is written here — 40 of the 45 hours — and PandaDoc drops to a signature-only plan wired into the platform through its API.
